In SCOPe 2.08, d1a14h2 (sunid 343393, 1a14 chain H residues 1-8) is not a normal protein domain. It is an N-terminal expression/purification tag segment, classified as sccs l.1.1.1. The path is class l (Artifacts) > fold l.1 (Tags) > superfamily l.1.1 (Tags) > family l.1.1.1 (Tags) > protein 'N-terminal Tags' (sunid 310894) > species 'Synthetic' (sunid 311501). The other part of chain H, d1a14h1 (residues 9-111, sunid 20061), is a real antibody variable domain in b.1.1.1 (Immunoglobulin fold, V-set). The same entry's d1a14l_ is also b.1.1.1, and d1a14n_ (neuraminidase) is b.68.1.1. The 1a14 entry is an NC10 anti-neuraminidase single-chain antibody complexed with influenza neuraminidase.

Similarity to the tag segment should NOT be treated as protein homology evidence. Class l is a bookkeeping category for artifacts: tags, linkers, engineered or expressed sequence that is not part of the native protein domain. The 'Tags' fold/superfamily/family is not an evolutionary grouping. It does not mean the segments share a common ancestor or a common fold, and the 'Synthetic' species label shows the sequence is engineered. A match to d1a14h2 or l.1.1.1 therefore only shows that both sequences carry a similar tag, vector or construct feature, for example a short peptide such as a His-tag or linker. It says nothing about the native protein's family, superfamily or function. The 8-residue segment is too short and too low in information to support any homology inference, and a shared tag can be attached to unrelated proteins. Evolutionary inference should rest on the real domain, d1a14h1 in b.1.1.1 (V-set immunoglobulin domain, a superfamily/family-level relationship), and only after proper sequence or structure comparison. The tag should be excluded from or masked in homology searches, template selection, representative-set building and benchmarking, and function should not be transferred through it. The split of chain H into h1 and h2 just reflects SCOPe separating the artifact residues from the true domain.
